observations.seen: A single warm sun from upper right gives readable form on the gate and towers, but the grass and tree canopies are lit almost flat. There is no visible rim or fill separation on the dark-clad player and enemy, so both read as near-silhouettes against the cobbles.

Trees, gate and characters cast sun shadows onto the path and grass with soft edges, which grounds the scene. Contact shadowing is weak under the bushes and buildings. The enemy relies on a flat beige disc decal instead of a real contact shadow, and the decal looks pasted on.
No environment reflection or sky-tinted specular is visible on any surface. The cobbles, wood and stone are all matte, and the shaded sides take no blue sky bounce.

The village set is coherent: a lacquered red gate, round stone towers with slate roofs, a half-timbered house, and distant hills. Beyond the props the grass plane is empty and uniform, with sparse bush placement and no ground clutter, flowers or path-edge blending.
Mild distance haze softens the hills and far roofs. There are no particles, light shafts, drifting leaves or other ambient motion cues for an outdoor day scene.

The cobblestone texture is the strongest material, with clear stone and grout definition. The tree canopies use a stretched, blotchy red texture on lumpy geometry that reads as painted clay. The grass is a low-detail tiling green, and the wood gate has little grain or roughness variation.

The tree canopies are faceted low-poly blobs with visible polygon edges at their silhouettes. The bushes are simple spheres. The characters are small and low-detail, with only an orange scarf distinguishing the player. The buildings are simple primitives with basic window cutouts.

The path leads strongly to the gate, which is centered, and the two foreground trees frame it. However, the canopies are oversized and eat the top corners under the HUD panels. The player sits low and small at roughly 10–12% of frame area, below the 18–25% target.

The camera is a behind-the-back chase view looking down the path, not the side-on follow camera the platformer recipe expects. The field of view looks near 50–60°, and the elevated angle reads the lane well.
No visible tone-mapping character, bloom, color grading or ambient occlusion. Colors are slightly muddy, the sky is a desaturated grey-blue, and the image has no daylight-outdoor grade punch.

Parchment-style panels with a serif typeface are consistent and readable, and the progress bar has named milestones. The labels crowd their values ('DISTANCE45 m', 'DEFEATED00'). The panels are heavy and cover the frame corners, and the ability grid adds clutter.
